body:
Draft. Do not merge without manual smoke. Routing stays **Shadow**; nothing deployed or installed.

Base: `mega/2026-09-29-consolidation` @ `8c003765` (contains the deployed signed build `237f54db` and the #1610-line scheduled-root Dayflow admission). This PR widens that admission instead of adding a parallel path.

## What this fixes

1. **Unattended runs held before the model ran.** Since the 2026-10-07 build, 72 AgentRunner sessions failed with `Dayflow provider guard held this request (history_ambiguous)`: 11 scheduled roots (now admitted on mega) plus scheduled child sessions and **61 self-improvement runs** that mega still holds. A session without an owner AND project can never receive Dayflow, so the existing zero-history ordinary path (`unbound`) now covers:
   - system AgentRunner sessions (`is_system=1`, `scheduled` or `self_improvement`, root or child; owner optional);
   - **owned** interactive chats left unassigned to a project (the app allows this; the deployed guard held them too, about 10% of chats in the week before the deploy).
   Retained Dayflow evidence, the non-reuse marker, archived or other-category rows and ownerless interactive rows stay `history_ambiguous`; a foreign owner stays `receiver_changed`; final exposure is rechecked; the Coordinator workflow path stays closed. No owners/projects invented; no DB patching. Shared validation now rejects a null session id (`RegExp#test(null)` matched). AgentRunner keeps the exact guard reason in run/schedule history and uses the generic Dayflow memory fence.
2. **Automatic memory injected unrelated context.** Semantic hits skipped every relevance check and the lexical gate scored whole notes. Every lane now needs >=2 content words shared between the request and the excerpt the model actually sees (+ atomic note title); broad notes (logs, indexes, synthesis, dated/import context, archive-tagged) need 3. Short follow-ups (<6 content words) use up to two recent substantive messages as relevance evidence (the search itself stays on the current message to keep Engraph fast); with none and <3 words, retrieval abstains. Budgets, header and untrusted fence unchanged. New SQLite-only, body-free per-turn receipts (`agent_memory_turn_receipts`, newest 200/session).
3. **Shadow model routing.** Never delays the turn (detached), evaluates `first_prompt` once per session, records the concrete would-be catalog pick without applying it, never lowers a frontier baseline on an unsure answer, records a body-free failure cause. Pins untouched.
4. **New router backend `openai_decisions`** (OpenAI Decisions API, `gpt-6-luna`): one ordered `score` question per first prompt (quick/everyday/hard); <0.15 cheap, >0.95 frontier. Write-only key, https + remote-data consent required (saving without consent is refused), tools/memories stay on the local reranker, failures leave the route unchanged. Electron router settings option.

Not addressed: the separate `nfl_mcp` required-MCP-unavailable scheduled failure.

## Verification

- `apps/api_server`: `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` exit 0. Router/Dayflow/memory/runner/permission suites 96 files / 1,196 passed; Dayflow suites after the final fix 372 passed (includes mega's `dayflow_scheduled_zero_history_admission` tests). Web typecheck 0; router settings browser contract 6/6 in Chrome (new `router:B7`: keyboard select, masked write-only key, consent-gated save, read-back, key-free test).
- Independent sandboxed verification gate on the pre-rebase head: all requested checks passed (API tsc; 325 router; 813 Dayflow/memory/runner; live 4+skip; web unit 81/81); its FAIL was evidence-only (browser proof of the new setting, now added; a wrong issue tag, removed). Full-suite `better-sqlite3` version failure and 5 `composer-model` browser failures reproduce on base.
- GitNexus: impact before edits (HIGH/CRITICAL on `AgentSessionMessagesRepository`, `runMigrations`, `normaliseDecisionSettings`, `DecisionSettings`; mitigated by additive-only changes and settings round-trip tests); `detect-changes` 0 affected processes, low.
- **Live, `tools/dev/sandbox.sh`** (synthetic fixture + scripted loopback provider; live ports untouched), final source `d7df02cd`:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| S1 ownerless scheduled run, no Dayflow | ran; real `pwd` output; no Dayflow text in what the model received |
| S2 same session with retained non-reuse marker | refused before dispatch; provider never called; marker unchanged |
| S3 scheduler resume of a marked session | skipped: schedules always create a new session (unit-tested) |
| S4 owned unassigned interactive chat + memory | answered; ordinary preference injected; Dayflow-tagged note absent; bare `resume` answered; provenance/receipts body-free |
| S5 harmless write | approval requested; file not written; rejected |
| R1 Kev shadow | classified once in background (turn 0.5 s, classifier 4.6 s); concrete would-be pick; session model unchanged. One cold-Kev 15 s timeout recorded before Kev warmed |
| R2 classifier down | `request_failed` / `ECONNREFUSED`; turn answered |
| R3 pinned session | never classified |
| R4 OpenAI Decisions shadow | once per session, frontier, 294 input tokens, ~1 s, concrete would-be pick; key absent from config/rows/logs |
| R5 no consent | backend cannot be saved (`consent_required`) |

**Installed app: not tested.** The signed 237f build still has the regression.

## Evaluation (aggregates; private detail kept off-repo)

- Memory, 115 real turns (deployed dist vs branch, copied DB + read-only Engraph copy): irrelevant-only turns 63 -> 32, turns with a useful lead 20 -> 19, memory step p50 325 -> 357 ms, budget unchanged. Misses: preferences that only exist inside a broad archive or share one word with the request.
- Router, 74 hand-labelled real first prompts (one judge, cross-validated thresholds): Decisions 55/74 (6 too small), Kev 50/74 (14), always-standard 46/74, current per-agent choices 38/74. Kev: cold first call 4.5 s, >15 s stalls after idle. Not enablement evidence.

## Kev (local System One)

Restored as a login service: `~/.local/share/kev/kev`, model `jaredpalmer/kev-4b@139fdd94` from the HF cache (offline), `127.0.0.1:8009`, launch agent `com.ajhochhalter.kev`, logs `~/Library/Logs/kev/`, ~10 GB RAM while loaded.

```bash
launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/com.ajhochhalter.kev | grep -E 'state|pid'            # status
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8009/v1/models | head -c 300                              # health + model
launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/com.ajhochhalter.kev                                # stop
launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.ajhochhalter.kev.plist # start
```

## Remaining limits

- Routing enablement needs a separate, evidence-backed decision; this PR keeps Shadow.
- Memory API cannot create user-owned notes; owner isolation is unit-tested only.
- Decisions thresholds/wording calibrated on one user's prompts with one judge.
- Engraph semantic timeouts are pre-existing (~45% since Oct 7) and grow with query length.

Record: `docs/ai/runs/2026-10-08-scheduled-dayflow-memory-router.md`. Decisions: `docs/ai/decisions/2026-10-08-unbound-session-dayflow-admission.md`, `docs/ai/decisions/2026-10-08-automatic-memory-displayed-text-relevance.md`.
title: fix: unattended Dayflow holds, memory relevance, non-blocking shadow routing + OpenAI Decisions backend

body:
## Scope (base: `mega/2026-09-29-consolidation`)
This PR brings **everything** from the deliverables branch onto mega, plus the coordinator multi-run work and the CI fixes. That's 63 commits on top of mega:
- **The 57 commits of `codex/rhythm-deliverables-completion-20261010`:**
  - the scheduled Dayflow/memory/router merge
  - the grid router core, plus showing and editing the Grid routing policy
  - qualification runtime isolation, so a qualification build never touches the user's opencode config, data or logs
  - engine-scope MCP reachability fixes
  - approval-expiry and auth fixes
  - seeded workflow skills
  - coordinator goal capture
  - the bounded coding layer's history
- **The coordinator multi-run work (below).** It retires the bounded coding layer again, so the final code has one coding path.
- **The Server CI repair:** the deliverables commits had broken 46 tests. These were stale or non-hermetic tests, plus one real `sandbox.sh` exit-status bug.

CI is green on this branch: server-checks, web-unit, type-check, foundation and postgres bootstrap. The slim port #1613 is superseded by this PR.

## What this does
One Coordinator chat (Secretary) now runs and tracks several coding jobs at once, using the **existing** workflow-orchestrator chain:

- **Start:** a goal like "fix X in /abs/path/to/repo" starts exactly one workflow-orchestrator run in its own engine git worktree and branch of that repo. The repo comes from your own goal text, not the model. A goal with no repo path is held and the Coordinator asks you for one.
- **Track:** `POST /coordinator-conversations/runs` plus a **Runs** tab in Details (only in a Rhythm Coordinator chat; nothing covers the transcript) show goal, branch (live `git HEAD`), Running / Needs you / Finished / Failed / Stopped, real tokens summed over the run and its sub-agents, and "reported in chat". It polls every 10s.
- **Act:** click a run to open its own session, to watch it or answer it. **Stop** (with an inline confirm) cancels the run via `POST /coordinator-conversations/runs/cancel`, aborts its whole session tree and withdraws its pending requests.
- **Notify:** when a background run (or one of its specialists) starts waiting on you, it pushes a "Rhythm needs you" bell notice. The desktop's existing clickable macOS banner for the request covers the native side, so there's no duplicate banner.
- **Report:** the existing exactly-once completion wake names each run's branch and worktree. The seeded workflow-orchestrator skill ends every run with **Changed / Branch & PR / Verification / Needs your decision**.
- **Approvals:** no new approval system. Runs use bypass mode confined to their worktree (`external_directory: deny` for the run and every specialist it delegates to; the #878 blocklist still applies). The existing taint approval on goal start stays; it only fires when the chat has read untrusted email or web content.

## Removed (one coding path left)
The bounded coding layer (`coordinator_coding_*`, grants, Docker protected evaluator, quickjs, the selectTasks fixture), the `rhythm_propose/start_bounded_coding_workflow` tools, the `coordinator.workflow.start` signed card, `chat_bounded_workflow` (including selected-reference summary), and the finite `workflow` purpose with its typed Coding Workflow adapter. About −14k lines. DB columns are left in place.

## Bugs found by the live demo and fixed here
- A run `cd`'d into the original checkout named in the goal and committed on `main`. Runs are now engine-confined to their worktree, and the run prompt points at the worktree.
- Two goals started together: the second start invalidated the first's bookkeeping, so the first run went untracked. Fixed, with a test.
- Starting a run no longer makes your next message fail as "stale".
- `tools/dev/sandbox.sh` could not run any Coordinator turn: `RHYTHM_MANAGED_CONTEXT_EXPORTS` was missing (Electron always sets it).

## Verification
- api/mcp/web typecheck and builds clean.
- api_server full suite: 29 failed vs 31 on base ff0e8c84, **no new failures**. mcp_server 224/224.
- Contract and coordinator tests 98/98; plan and contract are in `docs/ai/`.
- Live, in the isolated sandbox with your OpenAI sign-in (profiles on gpt-5.5):
  - Two goals ran concurrently, each on its own branch.
  - Each committed and passed `npm test` (re-run independently, 2/2 each).
  - Each reported once.
  - Original checkouts untouched.
  - A full runtime restart produced no duplicate reports and an identical run list.
- Env-gated live test `coordinator_workflow_runs_live.test.ts` passed against the sandbox.

Screenshot: `docs/ai/runs/evidence/2026-10-12-coordinator-runs-card.jpg`

## Manual smoke checklist (AJ)
Sandbox is still up: API 4098, engine 4097, web via the Browser pane at `http://127.0.0.1:4175`.
- [ ] Open **Rhythm**, then **Details → Runs**. The chat has no card over it.
- [ ] Send "Please fix <bug> in /private/tmp/rhythm-coord-demo/<repo> so its npm test passes" for two repos back to back. Both messages are accepted, without a "changed elsewhere" refusal.
- [ ] Runs shows both as **Running** on different `opencode/goal-…` branches, and tokens climb.
- [ ] Each finishes and the chat gets exactly one report per run with Changed / Branch / Verification / Needs your decision.
- [ ] `git -C /private/tmp/rhythm-coord-demo/<repo> log main` is unchanged, and the run branch has the fix.
- [ ] Click a run: its own session opens.
- [ ] Give Rhythm a goal whose run must use its question tool. Runs shows **Needs you — open to answer**, the bell gets "Rhythm needs you", and in the packaged app with Rhythm in the background a macOS banner appears. Clicking the run shows the question card.
- [ ] **Stop**, then **Yes, stop** on a running run: it shows **Stopped**, no report arrives, its "!" clears, and the original checkout is untouched.
- [ ] Send a coding goal with no repo path: the Coordinator asks for the path and starts nothing.
- [ ] Restart the runtime (`tools/dev/sandbox.sh restart` with the sandbox env, or Agents → Runtime → Restart in a packaged build). No report repeats, and the run list is identical.
- [ ] Optional, packaged: a qualification-only Electron build of this branch with a /private/tmp fixture manifest. Electron packaged smoke has **not** been run.

## Known follow-ups (not in this PR)
- The first Coordinator message right after a runtime restart can come back "uncertain" while the engine warms up, and the card's Retry only replays it.
- The fork still carries the schema-2 provider-guard protocol of the retired adapter.
- Not run: one web test that needs `apps/mobile` React, and `sandbox_attached_transport_contract_test.mjs`.

Never merge without AJ's smoke sign-off.

## What the user sees The Electron session inspector renders an empty context gauge: ``` 0 of 0 tokens 0% ``` The Flutter client, against the same account and the same live server, renders a full panel: ``` CONTEXT USAGE 150.7k / 1050k tokens 14% USAGE BUDGET ⟳ Anthropic — Team 5h limit 66% allowed · resets 1h weekly 30% allowed · resets 2d Anthropic — Personal 5h limit 100% allowed · resets 38m weekly 100% allowed · resets 4d OpenRouter credits 100% $0.00 / $20.00 Gemini quota fetch 401 OpenAI No usage API for the ChatGPT-plan token (standard API returns 401; Codex usage backend is undocumented). ``` The user's words: "the one with no information is what shows on electron, the one with helpful info is what is on flutter. make it like flutter." ## Root cause — the endpoint already exists and Electron never calls it This is the same shape as the Accounts gap fixed in `05ca632c`: working server capability, Flutter consumes it, the React renderer has no UI for it. `GET /agents/usage-budget` is mounted at `apps/api_server/src/app.ts:227` (`usageBudgetRouter` → `usage_budget_service.getUsageBudget`). Fetched live from the running instance it returns precisely the Flutter panel's contents: ```json {"providers":[ {"provider":"anthropic","label":"Anthropic — Team","kind":"window","accountId":"team", "items":[{"label":"5h limit","remainingFraction":0.66,"resetAt":"2026-09-21T22:10:00.000Z","detail":"allowed"}, {"label":"weekly","remainingFraction":0.30,"resetAt":"2026-09-24T02:00:00.000Z","detail":"allowed"}]}, {"provider":"anthropic","label":"Anthropic — Personal","kind":"window","accountId":"personal","items":[…]}, {"provider":"openrouter","label":"OpenRouter","kind":"credits", "items":[{"label":"credits","remainingFraction":1,"detail":"$0.00 / $20.00"}]}, {"provider":"gemini","label":"Gemini","kind":"unavailable","items":[],"reason":"quota fetch 401"}, {"provider":"openai","label":"OpenAI","kind":"unavailable","items":[], "reason":"No usage API for the ChatGPT-plan token (standard API returns 401; Codex usage backend is undocumented)."}], "fetchedAt":"2026-09-21T20:35:43.470Z"} ``` `grep -rn "usage-budget\|usageBudget" apps/web/src/` returns **zero matches**. No gateway method, no component, no call. Reference implementation to port from (behaviour, not Dart): - `apps/desktop_flutter/lib/features/agents/models/usage_budget.dart` — the response model; `provider` is one of `gemini | openrouter | anthropic | openai` - `apps/desktop_flutter/lib/features/agents/data/usage_budget_data_source.dart` — the fetch - `apps/desktop_flutter/lib/features/agents/views/_session_side_panel.dart` — the rendering the screenshot shows ## The separate half: context usage reads 0 / 0 `apps/web/src/components/Inspector.tsx:47`: ```tsx
{total.toLocaleString()}of {selected.totalBudget.toLocaleString()} tokens
{pct}%
``` The markup is fine; `total` and `selected.totalBudget` are both 0. Flutter shows `150.7k / 1050k · 14%` for the same session, so the numbers exist somewhere. **Determine where Flutter sources context usage before implementing** — it may come from the same endpoint, from session usage rows, or be derived from the model's context window. These are two distinct data paths and the issue should not assume they are one. Note also that Flutter abbreviates (`150.7k / 1050k`) while the Electron gauge calls `.toLocaleString()`, which would render `150,700 / 1,050,000`. Match Flutter's abbreviation. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] The Electron session inspector shows a Usage Budget panel populated from `GET /agents/usage-budget`. - [ ] All four provider shapes render correctly: `kind: "window"` (per-account limits with reset times), `kind: "credits"` (OpenRouter's dollar detail), `kind: "unavailable"` (the `reason` string shown as-is, e.g. Gemini's `quota fetch 401`), and multiple accounts of the same provider shown separately by `accountId` (Team vs Personal). - [ ] `resetAt` is rendered as a human-readable relative duration ("resets 1h", "resets 38m", "resets 2d"), not a raw ISO string — see #1565; use the shared formatter that issue introduces rather than adding another ad-hoc one. - [ ] A manual refresh control exists, matching Flutter's ⟳. - [ ] Context usage shows real numbers with Flutter's abbreviation (`150.7k / 1050k`), not `0 of 0` and not a comma-grouped full integer. The issue states where that data is sourced from. - [ ] `unavailable` providers are visually distinct from a 0% budget — an unavailable provider is not an exhausted one. - [ ] A failed `/agents/usage-budget` call degrades to a section-local error and does not blank the inspector (see #1559 for the shared-shell failure mode this must avoid). ## Notes - No server change is expected. If one turns out to be needed, say why. - Percentages here are `remainingFraction` — confirm the direction before rendering. Flutter shows Personal at 100% while unused, so the bar appears to represent *remaining*, not *consumed*. Getting this backwards would be silently wrong rather than visibly broken.
title: Electron session inspector shows an empty usage gauge; /agents/usage-budget is never called

## What the user sees A bordered row in the transcript containing a sparkle icon and the single word **"Reasoning"** — no body, no summary of what was reasoned about, nothing to read. It occupies a 40px band of the transcript and, when clicked, reveals an empty paragraph. ## Root cause `apps/web/src/gateway/sessions.ts:265` ```ts if (raw.type === 'reasoning') return { id, kind: 'reasoning', title: 'Reasoning', content: string(raw.text) }; ``` Every `reasoning` part is mapped to a block regardless of whether it carries text, and `apps/web/src/components/Transcript.tsx:25` renders it unconditionally: ```tsx
{block.title}{block.meta}

{block.content}

``` Empty reasoning parts are real and common — the engine emits a `reasoning` part as soon as a step begins and fills `text` later. Sampled a live session on `localhost:4001` (`/agent-sessions//messages`): **23 reasoning parts, 1 with `text: ""`** — the in-flight one, which is exactly what the user was looking at. Measured in the running fixture app: an empty `.reasoning-block` is **40px** tall (`summary` has `min-height: 38px`, `apps/web/src/styles.css:276`) and renders as a clickable affordance that reveals nothing. Two secondary problems in the same renderer: 1. `title` is hard-coded to the literal string `'Reasoning'`. The SDK text is already a headline — e.g. `**Planning repository indexing and state tracking**` — which would make a far more useful collapsed summary than the word "Reasoning" repeated down the transcript. 2. The body is rendered as plain text in a `

`, so that markdown shows up as literal asterisks. Other prose blocks go through `SafeMarkdown`. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] A `reasoning` part whose text is empty or whitespace renders nothing at all (no border, no row, no click target). - [ ] Reasoning text arriving later (live stream) still renders once it is non-empty. - [ ] The collapsed summary shows a useful label derived from the reasoning text (e.g. its first line / bold headline), falling back to "Reasoning" only when no such line exists. - [ ] Reasoning body renders through `SafeMarkdown` like other prose, so `**bold**` is not shown literally. - [ ] Test coverage for the empty-text case in `apps/web/tests/`. Files: `apps/web/src/gateway/sessions.ts:265`, `apps/web/src/components/Transcript.tsx:25`, `apps/web/src/styles.css:275-279`.
title: Transcript: empty "Reasoning" rows render as blank 40px bands; summary label is always the literal word "Reasoning"

## What the user sees

Under an in-progress assistant turn, the transcript prints:

```
Cost $0 · Input 0 · Output 0 · Cache read 0 · Cache write 0
```

Every number is zero, which reads like a reporting failure.

## Verdict: not a data bug — a presentation bug

Verified against live data on `localhost:4001` (`/agent-sessions/<id>/messages`):

- **Tokens are reported correctly for completed messages.** Same session, consecutive
  assistant messages: `input 31159 / output 22`, `input 3390 / output 91 / cache read 30976`,
  `input 21090 / output 405 / cache read 53376`, … Only the **last, still-running** message
  reports `input 0, output 0, cache 0`. The usage arrives when the message finishes.
- **Cost is real where the provider prices it.** Anthropic sessions report
  `cost: 0.10543375`, `0.0940935`, `0.0869084`, etc. The `openai / gpt-5.6-*` sessions
  report `cost: 0` for every message — plan/subscription pricing, not a bug.

So the footer in the screenshot is a *placeholder zero row for a message whose usage has
not arrived yet*, which the UI presents as though it were the final accounting.

## Root cause

`apps/web/src/components/Transcript.tsx:21`

```tsx
return message.cost !== undefined || message.tokens
  ? <small className="cost-line">{message.cost !== undefined && `Cost $${message.cost} · `}{message.tokens && `Input … Output … Cache read … Cache write …`}</small>
  : null;
```

The guard only checks for *presence*, not for meaningful values. The API always attaches a
`tokens` object and a numeric `cost` (`apps/web/src/gateway/sessions.ts:296-302`,
`apps/api_server/src/services/opencode_stream_bridge.ts:1566`), so the row always renders,
zeros included.

Separately, `` `$${message.cost}` `` is unformatted: a real value renders as
**`Cost $0.10543375`**.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The usage footer is not rendered while all token counts are zero/absent (in-flight message); it appears once real usage arrives.
- [ ] `Cost $0` is omitted when the provider reports no cost (plan-priced models), rather than printed as a literal `$0`.
- [ ] Cost is formatted to a sensible precision (e.g. `$0.11` / `$0.105`), never a raw float.
- [ ] Completed messages still show input / output / cache-read / cache-write exactly as the API reports them.
- [ ] Test in `apps/web/tests/` covering: in-flight message (no footer), plan-priced message (tokens shown, no cost), priced message (formatted cost).

Files: `apps/web/src/components/Transcript.tsx:21`, `apps/web/src/gateway/sessions.ts:296-302`.
title: Transcript: usage footer prints placeholder "Cost $0 · Input 0 · Output 0" for in-flight messages; cost is unformatted

## Problem
General availability requires adversarial validation, packaged-runtime evidence, documentation, and an immediate rollback switch.

## Dependencies
Depends on all preceding MCP Apps issues and successful Open Design plus `rhythm_get_dashboard` pilots.

## Scope
Add malicious fixtures, context/link/network/origin hardening, lifecycle pressure and crash recovery, packaged smoke coverage, docs, and `RHYTHM_MCP_APPS_MODE=off|readonly|interactive`.

## Non-goals
No SQL migration, unrelated Open Design compatibility work, extra MCP tools, or weakened restrictions.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Malicious matrix covers scripts, local/private networking, navigation, links, storage, oversized/flooded messages, stale nonces, proof replay, device permissions, and teardown abuse.
- [ ] Context updates are explicitly confirmed, bounded, scanned, taint-recorded, and fenced as untrusted.
- [ ] Packaged macOS enforces CSP/network/storage policies.
- [ ] Feature flag supports all three modes; `off` remains immediate rollback.
- [ ] Architecture, supported methods, operations, troubleshooting, and manual smoke are documented.
- [ ] Interactive mode stays opt-in until human smoke approval.

## Verification
- [ ] Full fork/API/Flutter/MCP suites and security fixtures.
- [ ] Isolated live behavioral suite.
- [ ] Packaged smoke for both pilots in all modes.
- [ ] Exact evidence recorded in `docs/ai/runs/`.

## Security / rollback
Any fail-open result blocks GA. No destructive migration is permitted.
title: MCP Apps: harden security and prepare GA rollout

body:
## Problem

Electron does not offer one coherent place to connect model providers and curate which models appear in agent/session pickers. Provider connection, catalog availability and model visibility are separate concepts, and the current UI does not give users the provider-first curation flow available in Hermes Desktop.

This is a UI/workflow issue. #1572 owns the catalog/filtering correctness underneath it; #1569 owns broader Hermes/Rhythm credential sharing.

## Hermes reference

Use the working Hermes Desktop interaction model as the product reference, especially:

- `apps/desktop/src/components/model-visibility-dialog.tsx`
  - searchable model list grouped by provider;
  - collapsible provider groups;
  - provider-level all/none checkbox;
  - per-model visibility switches;
  - family collapsing and readable model labels;
  - direct handoff to add/connect a provider.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/settings/model-settings.tsx`
  - provider readiness is honest (`authenticated` plus live models);
  - selecting an unconfigured provider opens the appropriate login/API-key/local-endpoint setup in place;
  - provider/model changes refresh from the live source of truth;
  - stale async responses cannot paint one profile's state into another.

Do not blindly copy Hermes implementation dependencies. Reuse Rhythm's existing components, provider auth endpoints, model catalog and visibility persistence while matching the proven flow.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Electron AI/Agent Settings has a clear provider-first screen showing connected, needs-login/key and unavailable states.
- [ ] An unconfigured provider can start its existing OAuth, API-key or local-endpoint setup without leaving the model workflow.
- [ ] Connected providers expose a searchable, scroll-contained list of their live models.
- [ ] Models can be enabled/hidden individually; each provider supports all/none selection and collapse/expand.
- [ ] Search matches provider, raw model ID and readable display name.
- [ ] Visibility persists through Rhythm's existing backend and refreshes every Electron model picker immediately without restart/session switch.
- [ ] Disconnected/unavailable models are not shown as selectable; currently selected stale/custom models remain visible with an honest warning until changed.
- [ ] Profile switching cannot leak catalog/login/visibility state from the previous profile.
- [ ] Keyboard navigation, focus containment, labels and narrow-window behavior meet the Hermes reference quality.
- [ ] Rendered tests cover login handoff, provider collapse/all-none, model toggle persistence, search and immediate picker refresh.
- [ ] Live sandbox evidence uses real catalog/provider responses; fixture-only rows are insufficient for final qualification.

## Likely Rhythm files

- `apps/web/src/components/tools/AgentSettingsTool.tsx`
- Electron/web provider account and profile/model settings surfaces
- `apps/web/src/gateway/sessions.ts`
- `apps/api_server/src/routes/agents_models_routes.ts`
- existing agent model visibility routes/data

## Dependencies

Coordinate with #1572 rather than creating a second filtering policy. The UI must consume the resolved catalog contract, not hard-code model generations.
title: Electron AI settings: add provider login and model curation modeled after Hermes Desktop
